speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are here for right flank pain and hematuria; to narrow this down, have you noticed any fever, nausea, or a history of kidney stones? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, CBC, BMP.

text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Reddish, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC Too numerous to count, Nitrites Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase Positive; Blood_Work: Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, BUN 14 mg/dL, Complete_Blood_Count Within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis confirms active urinary tract infection with significant hematuria, but the negative nitrites make a classic E. coli stone less likely. To determine if this is an obstructing stone or an infection-related kidney issue, do you have a history of passing kidney stones, and have you ever had a CT scan or ultrasound of your abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: You report a history of recurrent UTIs but no prior imaging; given your significant hematuria and flank pain, have you noticed any colicky pain radiating to the groin, and what is your personal or family history of kidney stones or smoking? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Pelvic_CT_NonContrast.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of recurrent infections is concerning for stones, but we need to rule out a malignancy given your age and significant hematuria. Do you have a history of smoking, and do you feel any mass in your abdomen or see any clots in your urine? REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Urography.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of recurrent infections, non-smoking status, and significant hematuria without gross clots, the risk of urothelial malignancy is lower, though we must still rule out a complex stone or abscess. Have you ever experienced fever, chills, or nausea/chills specifically with your flank pain? REQUEST IMAGES: CT_KUB.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right-sided Hydronephrosis secondary to a large renal calculus (kidney stone).
